drivingQuestion: With which formula should one take leave of a living companion?
outcomeNote: A dictum with two scriptural precedents; nothing is challenged.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין הַלֵּוִי: הַנִּפְטָר מֵחֲבֵרוֹ אַל יֹאמַר לוֹ ״לֵךְ בְּשָׁלוֹם״, אֶלָּא ״לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם״, שֶׁהֲרֵי יִתְרוֹ שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה ״לֵךְ לְשָׁלוֹם״, עָלָה וְהִצְלִיחַ. דָּוִד שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ לְאַבְשָׁלוֹם ״לֵךְ בְּשָׁלוֹם״, הָלַךְ וְנִתְלָה.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Avin HaLevi said: One who takes leave from another should not say to him: Go in peace, but rather,» he should say: «Go to peace. As we see» that, on the one hand, «Jethro said to Moses: “Go to peace”» (Exodus 4:18), and «Moses ascended and was successful.» On the other hand, «David said to» his son, «Absalom: “Go in peace”» (II Samuel 15:9), and Absalom «went and was» ultimately «hanged.»

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי אבין הלוי: הנפטר מחברו אל יאמר לו ״לך בשלום״
moves.summary: a further dictum of R' Avin HaLevi, on the formula of leave-taking
moves.about: Jethro's parting words to Moses as evidence for the right formula of leave-taking

moves.cueHe: שהרי יתרו שאמר לו למשה ״לך לשלום״
moves.summary: Moses prospered on לך לשלום, Absalom was hanged after לך בשלום
moves.about: David's parting words to Absalom as the counter-case
